decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding identify the same tested original study: Toste, Capin, Vaughn, Roberts, and Kearns (2017), 'Multisyllabic word reading instruction with and without motivational beliefs training for struggling readers in the upper elementary grades: A pilot investigation' (Elementary School Journal, 117(4), 593-615; DOI 10.1086/691684). The text explicitly identifies Toste, Capin, et al. (2017) as the original study whose three-condition intervention and findings are replicated, whereas Toste, Williams, and Capin (2017) is cited only for descriptive details of instructional components.

decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding assign 'mixed'. In the Replication Comparison and Replication Analysis sections, the authors explicitly report that effects on academic reading measures showed a similar pattern of positive treatment effects compared with Toste, Capin, et al. (2017) (though word reading fluency effect sizes were smaller and non-significant on TOWRE-2 Sight Word Efficiency), whereas the original findings regarding the embedded motivational beliefs (MB) training and reading motivation were not replicated (with no significant differences between MWR+MB and MWR-only and control students outperforming MWR+MB on reading motivation).

decisions.quote:
This randomized control trial examined the efficacy of an intervention aimed at improving multisyllabic word reading (MWR)
                                                                              skills among fourth- and fifth-grade struggling readers (n = 109, 48.6% male), as well as the relative effects of an embedded
                                                                              motivational beliefs training component. This study was a closely aligned replication of our earlier work. The intervention
                                                                              was replicated with a three-condition design: MWR only, MWR with a motivational beliefs component, and business-as-
                                                                              usual control.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding classify the study as a 'replication'. The paper reports a new randomized controlled trial with a new sample of 109 fourth- and fifth-grade struggling readers designed as a closely aligned replication of Toste, Capin, et al. (2017).
